- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- After a price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in the following 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤ 0.3), model frequently underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion or hidden demand.  
- Model consistently underestimates early in the 30-day horizon (e.g., days 1–5) when sentiment is low; adjust downward bias by +0.5–1.0% for first 3 days.  
- When sentiment history shows a recent spike (e.g., 1.00), model often fails to correct for mean reversion; apply a 1–2% downward adjustment in the 7–10 day window.  
- If model forecast is >75 and sentiment is 0.00, reduce forecast by 2–3% to avoid overconfidence in high volatility periods.
